prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: deployable portfolio website concept screenshot
Primary request: Create a polished desktop website mockup for a game developer portfolio that helps interviewers, recruiters, and first-time visitors quickly understand both the games and the developer. This is concept set B and should feel distinct from typical hero-page portfolios.
Scene/backdrop: full-browser website screenshot, realistic product mockup fidelity, no device frame
Subject: concept 1 of 5, assistant sidebar layout. Main content shows a bold games gallery with card thumbnails, role summaries, tech stack tags, and outcome-focused project highlights. A right-side chatbot panel is open as a contextual assistant that explains the developer's experience, strengths, and which game to inspect next.
Style/medium: high-fidelity modern web UI design, practical and shippable, memorable but not decorative noise
Composition/framing: 16:10-ish wide desktop page, clear header, left navigation, central project showcase, persistent right assistant rail, obvious information hierarchy
Lighting/mood: crisp, confident, product-design presentation
Color palette: warm ivory background, deep ink text, muted teal accents, amber highlights, restrained saturation
Materials/textures: subtle gradients, clean card surfaces, soft shadows, minimal glass effects
Text (verbatim): "Hong Jinho", "Games", "Role", "Tech", "Chatbot", "Strengths"
Constraints: make the chatbot clearly useful but not dominant; include sections for games, developer profile, technology, and chatbot; imply browsing flow from portfolio to assistant guidance; all UI text should be legible but concise; no watermark
Avoid: collage, mobile layout, fantasy UI, excessive neon, clutter, generic dribbble-style decoration
summary: Concept 01 uses a persistent assistant sidebar beside a strong games gallery so visitors can scan projects first and then ask for context about strengths, role, and next-step navigation.
generation_notes: Generated with the built-in image_gen tool in default mode. Selected as the sidebar-led concept for Set B because it foregrounds portfolio browsing while keeping the chatbot clearly useful and secondary.
